{{Short description|Spanish physicist and university teacher}}
[[File:PABLO ARTAL SORIANO WIKI2.jpg|alt=Pablo Artal|thumb|Pablo Artal]]
'''Pablo Artal''' (born June 12, 1961, in [[Zaragoza]]) is a Spanish [[physicist]] and [[Full Professor|full professor]] specialized in [[optics]] at the [[University of Murcia]], as well as in the development and application of new techniques in human vision research. He is the founder and director of the Optics Lab at Murcia University <ref>https://lo.um.es</ref> and received the Spanish National Research award "Juan de la Cierva" and the [[Rey Jaime I Awards|Rey Jaime I Award]] for New Technologies in 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.fprj.es/semblanza-de-los-siete-ganadores-de-los-premios-rey-jaime-i-2015/|title=Semblanza de los siete ganadores de los Premios Rey Jaime I 2015|date=2 June 2015|publisher=Fundación Premio Rey Jaime I|language=es|access-date=20 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305104004/http://www.fprj.es/semblanza-de-los-siete-ganadores-de-los-premios-rey-jaime-i-2015/|archive-date=5 March 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://lo.um.es/member/pablo-artal/|title=Pablo Artal|publisher=Laboratorio de Óptica-Universidad de Murcia|access-date=20 May 2016}}</ref> His main research topics are the optics of the eye and the retina and the development of optical and electronic imaging techniques in the field of biomedicine, ophtalmology and vision.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://pabloartal.blogspot.com/|title=Pablo Artal Blog|language=en|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> He has contributed to the advance of methods for the study of the optics of the eye and contributed to the understanding of the factors that limit the resolution of the human vision. Moreover, his discoveries and ideas have been applied to instruments and devices used in the clinical practice of ophthalmology.

== Biography ==
After earning a MSc degree in physics from the [[University of Zaragoza]], he joined the [[Institute of Optics]] of the [[Spanish National Research Council|Higher Council of Scientific Research (CSIC)]] located in Madrid as a PhD student in 1984. His PhD supervisor was Javier Santamaria. After his doctorate he was a post-doctoral fellow at the [[University of Cambridge]], [[United Kingdom|UK]] and the  [[Institut d'Optique Graduate School|Institut d'Optique]], [[Orsay]] (France).

Back to Spain, he became a permanent researcher at the Institute of Optics ([[Spanish National Research Council|CSIC]]). Since 1994 he has been the first Full Professor of Optics at the [[University of Murcia]], and was the funder of the Optics Laboratory.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://politica.elpais.com/politica/2015/10/02/actualidad/1443809170_325008.html|title=El Rey: "Los Jaime I son un motivo de confianza en nuestro futuro común"|date=15 October 2015|newspaper=El País|language=es|access-date=20 May 2016|last1=Alberola |first1=Miquel }}</ref> He is also an elected fellow member of the [[The Optical Society|Optical Society of America]] (OSA), fellow of the Association for research in Vision and Ophthalmology (ARVO) and the European Optical Society (EOS). He is a member of the Academy of Sciences of the Region of Murcia and the Academy of Medicine and a distinguished visiting professor at the [[Central South University]] in Changsha (China).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.laverdad.es/ababol/ciencia/convenio-central-south-20181103010953-ntvo.html|title=Convenio con la Central South University de Changsa|date=2018-11-05|website=La Verdad|language=es|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref>

He was awarded with the [[Edwin H. Land Medal]]  by the OSA and the Society for Imaging Science and Technology (IS&T), "For scientific contributions to the advancement of diagnostic and correction alternatives in visual optics" (2013).<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://lo.um.es/prof-pablo-artal-received-the-prestigous-edwin-h-land-medal-award/|title=Prof. Pablo Artal received the prestigious Edwin H Land medal award {{!}} Laboratorio de Óptica. Universidad de Murcia|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> The [[European Research Council]] granted Artal with an Advanced Research grant in 2014 with a total budget of 2.5 million euros for the creation of optoelectronic glasses.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.europapress.es/murcia/noticia-consejo-europeo-investigacion-concede-pablo-artal-25-millones-euros-crear-gafas-optoelectronicas-20130928112937.html|title=El Consejo Europeo de Investigación concede a Pablo Artal 2,5 millones de euros para crear unas gafas optoelectrónicas|date=2013-09-28|publisher=Europa Press|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> He received the 'Rey Jaime I' Award for New Technologies in 2015. The mention states that he hold more than 20 international patents and was founder of five companies in the field of optics... [which] has helped to improve the quality of life of people around the world." In May 2016, he announced that he dedicated 20,000 of the 100,000 euros obtained from the Rey Jaime I to support ten scholarships for the most talented undergraduate students enrolled in the science degrees at the University of Murcia.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://elpais.com/elpais/2016/05/17/ciencia/1463487113_392269.html|title=Un científico gana un premio y dona 20.000 euros a estudiantes brillantes|last=Ansede|first=Manuel|date=18 May 2016|language=es|access-date=20 May 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.elperiodicodearagon.com/noticias/aragon/fisico-zaragozano-pablo-artal-dona-20-000-euros-becas_1111696.html|title=El físico zaragozano Pablo Artal dona 20.000 euros para becas|date=18 May 2016|publisher=elperiodicodearagon.com|language=es|access-date=20 May 2016}}</ref> Artal won the Juan de la Cierva Spanish National Research Award in 2018<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.um.es/web/sala-prensa/-/pablo-artal-candidato-al-premio-nacional-de-investigacion-juan-de-la-cierva-en-el-area-de-transferencia-de-tecnologia|title=El investigador de la Universidad de Murcia Pablo Artal gana el Premio Nacional de Investigación - Nota de prensa - Sala de prensa - Universidad de Murcia|website=www.um.es|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> and the [[Edgar D. Tillyer Award|Edgar D. Tillyer award]] of the OSA for “the pioneering use of optics and [[photonics]] technologies to unravel the human visual system and to improve eye diagnostics and correction”.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://lo.um.es/pablo-artal-receives-the-2019-edgar-d-tillyer-award-from-osa/|title=Pablo Artal receives the 2019 Edgar D. Tillyer Award from OSA {{!}} Laboratorio de Óptica. Universidad de Murcia|language=en-GB|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> He was the recipient of the Gold Medal of the Royal Spanish Society of Physics.

Artal is co-inventor of 35 patents in the Optics and Ophtalmology fields <ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.linkedin.com/in/pabloartal/?originalSubdomain=es|title=Pablo Artal profile|website=LinkedIn}}</ref> and the co-founder of two spin-off companies (Voptica SL & Visiometrics SL) focused on optical solutions{{buzzword inline|date=September 2019}} and diagnostic instruments.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://cienciaysalud.laverdad.es/la-ciencia/ciencia-actual/que-hacen-pablo-artal-su-loum-article.html|title=¿Qué hacen Pablo Artal y su LOUM? - Ciencia actual - La Ciencia - Ciencia y Salud - laverdad.es|website=cienciaysalud.laverdad.es|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> According to [[Google Scholar]], he has published more than 400 scientific studies with more than 25200 citations and with a h-index of 85.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=L2qYVBgAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Pablo Artal - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> He has participated in more than 300 invited presentations in international meetings and approximately 300 seminars in scientific institutions across the world.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1q80DgAAQBAJ&q=artal+150+seminars+in+research+institutions+around+the+world&pg=PR9|title=Handbook of Visual Optics, Volume Two: Instrumentation and Vision Correction|last=Artal|first=Pablo|date=2017-02-24|publisher=CRC Press|isbn=9781482237931|language=en}}</ref> He edited the two-volume “Handbook of Visual Optics” in 2017.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crcpress.com/Handbook-of-Visual-Optics-Volume-One-Fundamentals-and-Eye-Optics/Artal/p/book/9781482237856|title=Handbook of Visual Optics, Volume One: Fundamentals and Eye Optics|website=CRC Press|language=en|access-date=2019-06-22}}</ref> In May 2026, he edited the second edition of the Handbook of Visual Optics. In 2026, Artal published "I Have Cataracts: What Should I Know?", a patient-oriented guide explaining cataracts and their treatment from the perspective of an optical scientist.

Some of his inventions are already present in the clinical practice: the [[adaptive optics]] visual simulator (VAO) http://voptica.com and a new type of intraocular lenses with inverted meniscus shape that improves the quality of vision in the periphery (ArtIOLs).<ref>{{cite journal | url=https://journals.healio.com/doi/10.3928/1081597X-20230802-01 | doi=10.3928/1081597X-20230802-01 | title=Visual Performance at All Distances and Patient Satisfaction with a New Aspheric Inverted Meniscus Intraocular Lens | date=2023 | last1=Marín | first1=José M. | last2=Hervella | first2=Lucía | last3=Villegas | first3=Eloy | last4=Robles | first4=Consuelo | last5=Alcón | first5=Encarna | last6=Yago | first6=Inés | last7=Artal | first7=Pablo | journal=Journal of Refractive Surgery | volume=39 | issue=9 | pages=582–588 | pmid=37675912 | doi-access=free }}</ref>
